activity_statements.statement: designs and manufactures aerospace and defense products through Collins Aerospace, including electric power systems, flight control systems, avionics, engine nacelles, and aircraft interiors for commercial and military customers
designs, produces, and services commercial and military aircraft engines through Pratt & Whitney, including engines for the F-35 and A320neo family
develops and manufactures advanced defense systems through Raytheon including missile systems, radar systems (SPY-6 family), and electronic warfare capabilities for military customers
provides aftermarket maintenance, overhaul, spare parts, and technical support for commercial airlines and government customers through Collins Aerospace and Pratt & Whitney service organizations
produces critical munitions, decoy systems (MALD), and electronic warfare systems for US and allied military forces
serves commercial and government customers in original equipment and aftermarket segments across the aerospace industry in 150+ countries

name_reality_gap: RTX is indexed as 'Aviation and Aerospace Component Manufacturing,' which significantly understates its defense role. Raytheon (one of RTX's three segments) is a major prime defense contractor building missiles, radars, and electronic warfare systems — it is as much a weapons manufacturer as an aerospace parts company. The RTX corporate rebrand from Raytheon Technologies obscures the defense weapons heritage.
extraction_notes: RTX main website pages (who-we-are/our-company, our-businesses) returned 404 or timed out. Raytheon segment page loaded. RTX 10-K accessed via ExaSearch provided detailed segment descriptions for Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney, and Raytheon. Segment weights are approximate equal split based on known RTX reporting.
